newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks recover some losses, but end down.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks recover some losses, but end down.

* Toronto stocks recovered from midday losses of around two percent, but ended the session 1.23 percent lower on Monday on rate jitters and fallout from the Bre-X Minerals Ltd saga.
Toronto stocks recovered from midday losses, but still ended the day 1.23 percent lower on interest rate fears and fallout from Bre-X Minerals Ltd.

The TSE 300 key composite index fell 81.53 points to 5850.22 on turnover of 74.94 million shares for a value of C$1.21 billion. Advancing stocks trailed declining stocks 264 to 739 with 294 stocks unchanged.

Traders said investor jitters remained dominant in the market amid confusion over the Bre-X situation and the belief that a 25-basis point hike in interest rates last week by the U.S. Federal Reserve could be matched by another in May.
"It's the Bre-X fears, the higher interest rate fears and you've got a very nervous market here," said Josef Schachter of Schachter Asset Management Inc.
Schachter said there is probably another 100 to 200 points worth of losses to come, but a recovery could come from first quarter earnings reports due to begin appearing next week.
"Right now the market is running on fear and with the quarter's end there is probably a ton of dumping going on as people blow positions away."
Banks and brokerages led the fall for sub-indices on the Toronto as the Financial Services index slid 2.14 percent.
Analysts said the possibility of higher U.S. rates could mean thinner bottom lines for Canadian banks as spreads widen and speculation emerges about possible interest rate rises in Canada.
HOT STOCKS
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd shares were halted, but the exchange said on Monday that it plans to resume trading on Tuesday.

The company issued a statement earlier, urging the Toronto exchange to keep the shares halted until a study by Freeport- McMoran Copper and Gold Inc was completed and Strathcona Minerals, Bre-X's consultant completed an audit of earlier drilling results. Traders said the "sheer number of orders" backlogged on the stock should spur another active session for the small miner.
((Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100))
